newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican construction jobs up 4.3 pct yr/yr in Feb.
newsitem.headline: Mexican construction jobs up 4.3 pct yr/yr in Feb.

text.p: Employment in the Mexican construction sector grew by 4.3 percent in February compared to the same month a year earlier, the National Statistics Institute (INEGI) said on Wednesday.
The number of office workers in the construction sector grew by 5.7 percent while the number of laborers grew by 3.9 percent, INEGI said in a statement.
The statement, based on companies that are part of the National Construction Chamber (CNIC), reported only percentages and not raw numbers.
It did not include any figures on the total value of construction.
As reported in Mexican industrial activity data on April 15, real production in the construction industry rose 9.6 percent in February compared to the same month in 1996, the report said.

In the month of February, 35.3 percent of all construction works were classified under general building, 18.3 percent for transportation, 16 percent for the petroleum and petrochemicals sector, 9.1 percent for water, sewer and irrigation projects, and 7.7 percent for electricity and communications.
The category "other construction" accounted for 13.6 percent, the report said.
